summary: Missouri Conservation Commission lookout at Drake, Gasconade County: towersite bought 1950-51, tower erected 1952-53, 1953 fire; no later record found.

staffing.status: ranger on duty at the Drake lookout tower

events.note: FY 1950-51: an 11.36-acre towersite acquired (page quotes Missouri Conservation Commission annual report)
FY 1952-53: a new tower erected at the Drake towersite (page quotes Missouri Conservation Commission annual report FY 1952-53)
October 1953 woodland fire spotted by the ranger at the Drake lookout tower; nearly 10 acres burned (1953 New Haven Leader item, quoted on the page)

evidence.supports: Missouri Conservation Commission operated the Drake lookout, Gasconade County

evidence.quote: FY 1950-51: A 11.36 acre towersite was acquired.

evidence.quote: FY1952-53: A new tower was erected at the Drake towersite.

evidence.quote: It was thought that the fire was started from some careless hunters making a fire inside a large, hollow green tree.

notes_for_editor: Status, access and present condition are not in any source read, so they are left out. The page quotes Missouri Conservation Commission annual reports (FY 1950-51, FY 1952-53) that were not opened; the FY dates are kept as printed. 'A new tower was erected' may imply an earlier tower on the towersite, but no source says so. Two WebSearch queries, the 2020 Gasconade Hills Conservation Area plan (missouriconservation.com, no mention of Drake or a tower) and firetower.org (no Drake entry) gave nothing further. The MDC article is general background only. Brief's agency and county agree with the page; height stays null because no source gives one.
